subject.title: MCP: render large JSON tool outputs as structured artifacts/previews

question: Should OpenClaw add a generic core tool-result artifact/preview contract for oversized structured outputs, or keep result shaping and presentation owned by individual plugins and clients?
rationale: Current seams cover generic artifacts, JSON result creation, and MCP normalization separately; choosing automatic capture thresholds, persistence scope, privacy behavior, agent visibility, and Control UI rendering defines a durable cross-surface contract.

options.title: Sponsor a generic result contract
options.body: Define an owner-neutral tool-result summary/artifact reference contract, then implement MCP and Control UI adoption behind focused tests.

options.title: Keep result ownership local
options.body: Document that MCP servers or plugins must summarize and attach their own results, avoiding new core persistence and UI policy.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a generic result contract
recommendation.body: Define an owner-neutral tool-result summary/artifact reference contract, then implement MCP and Control UI adoption behind focused tests.

likelyOwner.reason: The repository vision supplies the decisive core-versus-extension and pragmatic MCP boundary.
